Class EquinixIXMapping

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.design.peering.model.EquinixIXMapping
public class EquinixIXMapping extends Object
Bridges PeeringDB Equinix IX and facility IDs to Equinix Fabric MetroId values entirely from live data — no hardcoded city table.

Equinix names every IBX (facility) with its metro as a prefix — LA3/LA4 are in Los Angeles, SV5 in Silicon Valley, DC11 in Ashburn. So a facility is resolved by reading the IBX code out of its PeeringDB name and looking it up in the live IBX→metro map supplied at construction (built from fabric.metros().getIbxs()); an exact IBX hit wins, and the metro prefix is a fallback (accepted only when it names a metro present in the live map, so a brand-new metro resolves while a stray token does not). Each resolved facility also seeds a city→metro map, through which IXes — which carry only a city — resolve. This means even city aliases (a "San Jose" exchange co-located with the Silicon Valley SV facilities) map correctly, with no static table and without depending on coordinates.

Because the bridge is keyed by MetroId (not the MetroCode enum), a metro that is live in Fabric but not yet in the enum still resolves and stays distinct.

Call mapFacilities(Map) before mapIxes(Map) (the IX bridge depends on the facility pass).

    • resolveFromName

      public MetroId resolveFromName(String name)
      Reads an Equinix IBX code out of a name (e.g. "Equinix LA4 - Los Angeles") and resolves it to a metro: an exact match against the live IBX→metro map wins; otherwise the IBX's metro-code prefix is tried, accepted only when that prefix names a metro present in the live map.
      Parameters:
      name - a PeeringDB facility name (or aka)
      Returns:
      the resolved metro, or null if the name carries no recognizable IBX code
